In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
(+)-(18-C6)-2, 3, 11, 12-tetracboxylic acid is a good chiral tethering unit for the preparation of a new chiral stationary phase.

the chiral tethering effect of (+)-(18-crow-6)-2.3,11, 12-tetracarbonylic acid is very important and significant in the chiral recognition of N-(3.5-dinitro-benzoyl)-1 -phenylalkylamine and N-(3. 5-dinitro benzoyl)-α- amino acid derivatives.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a chiral tethered CSP can show an enantioselectivity different from those of the two chirogenic units constituting the CSP.

the chiral tethering groups can be used for the preparation of CSPs having high chiral recognition abilities and that the use of a chiral tethered CSP can provide a simple method for the preparation of a CSP with high chiral recognition ability.

the chiral recognition mechanism of the CSPs based on a chiral tethered group and chiral unit(s) depends on the cooperative or uncooperative interaction between the chiral tethering groups and chiral units(s).

(+)-(18-CROWN-6)-2.3,11, 12-tetracarbolic acid can be successfully utilized as a chiral linker to prepare new CSPs.
the use of a crown ether as a chiral linker can be an effective strategy for the preparation of CSPs with high enantioselectivity.
